problem.text: In base $10$, the number $2013$ ends in the digit $3$. In base $9$, on the other hand, the same number is written as $(2676)_9$ and ends in the digit $6$. For how many positive integers $b$ does the base-$b$-representation of $2013$ end in the digit $3$?

steps.title: Where to start: the last digit is a remainder
steps.body: The problem shows you two examples: $2013$ ends in $3$ in base $10$ and in $6$ in base $9$. That is no accident. In base $b$, every digit except the last one stands for a multiple of $b$, so the last digit is exactly the remainder when the number is divided by $b$.

your_turn.prompt: Check the base $9$ example: what is the remainder when $2013$ is divided by $9$?
your_turn.answer: $9\cdot 223 = 2007$, so the remainder is $2013 - 2007 = 6$, the last digit of $(2676)_9$.

steps.title: Turn the condition into divisibility
steps.body:
We want the remainder of $2013$ divided by $b$ to be $3$. Then $2013 = kb + 3$ for some whole number $k$, so $b$ must divide $2013 - 3$:
$$b \mid 2010.$$ Keep in mind that a remainder of $3$ also needs $b$ to be bigger than $3$; we will use that at the end.

your_turn.prompt: Is $b = 10$ one of the bases that work? Use the divisibility test.
your_turn.answer: Yes. $10$ divides $2010$, and indeed $2013$ ends in $3$ in base $10$.

steps.title: Count the divisors of 2010
steps.body: Factor $2010 = 2\cdot 3\cdot 5\cdot 67$. To count divisors, add $1$ to each exponent and multiply. Every exponent here is $1$, so each prime is either in a divisor or not.

your_turn.prompt: How many positive divisors does $2010$ have?

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: Careful: not all $16$ divisors are allowed. In base $b$ the digits are $0$ to $b-1$, so the digit $3$ exists only when $b \ge 4$. The divisors $1$, $2$ and $3$ of $2010$ are too small (for example, $2013$ divided by $3$ leaves remainder $0$, not $3$). Every other divisor is at least $5$ and works. That leaves $16 - 3 = 13$ bases. The answer is **(C)**.

wrong_choices.D: This is the number of divisors of $2010$, but it forgets that bases $1$, $2$ and $3$ have no digit $3$. Those three must be removed.
